Sam (Support): FYI — incoming ticket from AcmePay: tool/function call args sometimes come through truncated when client uses SSE streaming to our hosted API. Customer sees JSON parse errors. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d
Priya (Customer): Repro attached. We call the charge tool via streaming and intermittently get `Unexpected end of JSON input` when the client tries to parse the tool args. Snippet we see on our side: ```data: {"tool":"charge", "args": {"amount": 100, "currency": "USD", "order_id": "ord_12345"``` (no closing braces)
Sam (Support): Customer says they sent full JSON. On our side the event data is missing the trailing `}}`. Client stack: browser EventSource; server API: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream; edge: Fastly in eu-west-1.
Miguel (Engine Runtime): Can you paste gateway logs + exact chunk sizes? Also which SDK version?
Sam (Support): Logs for req_0a1b2c3d: ```ERROR parse_tool_args: EOF at pos 158
SSE chunks (bytes): [1024, 512, 16]
Last chunk payload (raw): "...,\"order_id\":\"ord_12345\"\n"```
Lin (SRE): Hypothesis: TCP/proxy writes split the SSE `data:` payload mid-JSON; the browser EventSource will present `data:` lines concatenated but some client parsers assume a single `data:` chunk contains complete JSON. We need to be resilient to `data:` being split across frames.
Miguel (Engine Runtime): Agreed. Short-term workaround: wrap tool args payload in base64 so any split doesn't break JSON, or send an explicit sentinel event `event: tool-eof` after the last chunk. Long-term: runtime should buffer `data:` lines for toolcall events until a valid JSON parse is possible or a configurable EOF marker is received.
Sam (Support): Customer accepted base64 workaround and is unblocked. They requested engineering fix so they can stop using the hack.
Miguel (Engine Runtime): I'll take this. Plan: add buffering layer in streaming parser specifically for `tool_call` events. Also add unit tests that simulate arbitrary chunk boundaries, and a flag `streaming_toolcall_mode: assembled|passthrough` in config.
Sam (Support): Repro steps I used: 1) open SSE to /v1/stream; 2) push a toolcall whose JSON is split across TCP writes; 3) observe parse error. Minimal repro script below.
Sam (Support): ```bash
# split-sse-repro.sh — intentionally split JSON across writes
HOST=api.redwood.ai
PORT=443
(
  printf "event:tool\n"
  printf "data: {\"tool\":\"charge\",\"args\":{\"amount\":100,\"currency\":\"USD\",\""; sleep 0.15
  printf "\"order_id\":\"ord_12345\"}}\n\n"
) | nc -N $HOST $PORT
```
Miguel (Engine Runtime): Nice repro. I'll create an internal issue with logs + script. Would help to know if the truncated cases correlate with client keepalive intervals or with Fastly buffering settings.
Lin (SRE): I'm going to scan recent Fastly config changes and add a metric: `toolcall_parse_error` grouped by chunk_count and edge_service. If we see a bump correlated with chunk_count > 3 we can confirm.
Sam (Support): Customer contact: Priya (AcmePay). They've agreed to keep base64 workaround until we deploy a fix.
Miguel (Engine Runtime): Filing now, assigning to `eng-runtime` and tagging `sre` for edge investigation. I'll propose a short-term parser buffer + tests and a follow-up config option.
deploy-bot: Triggered pipeline for branch `fragments-parse-fix` against non-prod.
Sam (Support): Marking this escalated — please post issue link here when available. Thanks :pray:
Miguel (Engine Runtime): Will do. I'll post issue/PR in ~2 hours with initial tests and a proposed config.
